questions.question: Why did Aurora Beverages’ change from a 28mm to a 26mm bottle neck require involvement from both the F&B and CNC divisions, and which CNC work order was used for the new tooling?
questions.why: The reason is in the F&B procedure; the work order number is only in the CNC tooling spec. Close to CD1, which top-3 retrieval misses.

questions.question: How did the Aurora Beverages June 2026 rush order affect CNC’s production schedule, and what happened to external Order C-4471 as a result?
questions.why: The whole answer is in the CNC capacity report, so it does not test cross-division synthesis. Contains the order id C-4471, which makes keyword retrieval easy.

questions.question: How did the Jewellery division financially support the F&B division’s expansion for the Aurora rush order, including the amount financed and repayment period?
questions.why: The Jewellery treasury report states the mechanism, amount and term. fnb-06 states the amount and term too, so either document would answer it.

questions.question: What pricing components were included in custom commission JWL-Q-3391, and what was the final quoted total?
questions.why: A five-item list plus a total from one quote; tests completeness. Contains the job id JWL-Q-3391.

questions.question: What six checks must be completed during a 500-unit pilot run under QC-FNB-002 before the batch can be cleared for full-line rollout?
questions.why: A six-item list from one checklist; every item must appear. Same document as main S8. Contains the document id QC-FNB-002.

questions.why: Absent but plausible: the documents give revenue and financing figures but no cost by division, so the right answer is that the documents do not say.
